title: Volume 2 Chapter 3: Howling for You Who Cannot Cry 2
content: "That is..."
I wrapped my left hand around the right hand I had peeled away, holding it close to my chest as if in prayer, not wanting to let anything escape.
"Isn't that just a rationalization?"
Erika laughed as if she had resigned herself to the situation.
Thanks to Erika's Healing Magic, my body was in perfect condition.
I had consumed quite a bit of magical power, but since I could only properly use efficient body enhancement and Healing Magic, it shouldn't be a problem.
As I stood up, I thanked my sword in my heart while returning it to its sheath.
It was a good sword; it had kept me alive.
Erika, who stood up in the same manner, wore a wry smile.
"While I did say we should share our difficulties, it seems I've put all the burden on you this time."
I suddenly wondered if the reason Erika was angry was because I had fought the Great Demon Knight, a rare monster, all by myself.
In other words, it was unfair to fight a rare monster alone.
Indeed, battling a rare monster was a valuable experience for adventurers.
No, don't think too deeply about it, me. Let's just brush it off; there are things I need to say.
"I'll be more careful from now on. We should share the burden properly."
Erika raised an eyebrow skeptically at my words.
"Well, if we have time, I could explain just how seriously I'm trying to uphold our marital vows."
I looked straight into Erika's eyes.
She met my gaze with a serious expression.
"We don't have time."
Would she believe my words?
"Perhaps Sister Shara is the enemy."
What Erika swallowed was either a joke or a "no way."
It was concerning, but at least Erika didn't outright deny my words.
"Why do you think that?"
Instead, a straightforward question emerged.
"Because she's the only one who can do it."
Erika rolled the words "she's the only one who can do it" around in her mouth.
"Didn't you find it strange, Erika? Why are there so few monsters? There were so many when we entered the forest."
"Yes, I did find that odd."
"The reason is that they escaped from that."
I pointed to the Great Demon Knight, now a pile of magical stone debris.
"That is not a monster that should appear here."
Erika tilted her head slightly at my words.
If that monster is occurring in the mid-level of the Demon Realm, it means that adventurers who accidentally entered might encounter it.
I hesitated to continue for a moment.
What if she thought I was an arrogant human?
"Right now, in Hekatai, it's impossible to stop the forest's expansion. There simply aren't enough strong fighters."
What was I saying? I braced myself, wondering what she would think if she thought I was just some nobody. Erika spoke.
"Is that your assessment?"
At least I felt relieved that there was no hint of contempt in her voice.
I've been observing since we arrived in Hekatai.
There were strong fighters, and some I couldn't even recognize.
But their numbers are far too few.
At the very least, we don't have enough to prevent encounters with the Oganite.
"I see, that's your assessment. I'll believe you, as it seems I have a habit of misjudging people's true worth."
Erika responded with a hint of irony in her tone.
"Then, where did that thing come from?"
"From deeper within—"
"Yes, from the depths."
Riding the momentum of Erika's words, I continued.
Why did we encounter a horde of monsters right after entering the forest?
Because the mid-level monsters were fleeing to the shallower areas.
Why didn't we meet other adventurers in the mid-level?
Because they were too busy dealing with the monsters overflowing from the forest.
All of it was circumstantial evidence.
It was a discussion about monsters, and if someone said it just happened to be that way, I couldn't deny it.
Why would that happen?
Because someone lured that thing out from the depths.
Why would they pull a monster from the depths, which would likely require significant sacrifices, to the mid-level?
Because there was someone they wanted dead today.
I thought Erika would understand what I was trying to say, but I finished my thought anyway.
Then, who knew that the person they wanted dead would come here today?
And who could lead that person to the very spot they targeted?
I didn't finish my sentence because Erika answered before I could.
"The Church, and the one who was closest and had been with them until just before was none other than Shara."
Erika let out a breath that resembled a sigh.
"As a member of the nobility, I believe I'm accustomed to deception. But feeling nothing is still difficult."
As a failure among the nobility, I had no comforting words for her.
I couldn't feel anger at being deceived, nor could I accept that I had grown accustomed to betrayal.
So, when I sensed that presence, my face stiffened slightly.
Was it because I had no comforting words to offer myself?
Or was it anger towards those assassins?
I couldn't tell.
Before I knew it, a masked figure stood next to the pile of magical stone debris from the Great Demon Knight.
The hair spilling from the robe that covered their entire body was reminiscent of Shara's golden locks, who was not here.
"You useless fool."
The masked figure said this as they kicked the remains of the Great Demon Knight, the pile of magical stone debris.
In Hekatai, the adventurer Barrel shouted orders at the top of his lungs for what felt like the umpteenth time today.
He was supposed to be hunting monsters in the Demon Realm's grasslands to earn some pocket change, just like any other day.
He had no intention of entering the forest, aiming for a safe and easy day.
That was the plan.
The once ordinary grasslands of the Demon Realm transformed into a desperate battlefield in just an hour.
He couldn't make sense of it. But there was no time to think.
A massive horde of monsters spilled out of the forest.
As someone who had grown up in the territory of the Marquis Makikomaru, he couldn't help but recall the events from sixty years ago.
Would something like that happen again? Last time, literally half of Hekatai's adventurers had died.
That sense of crisis seemed to be a common fear among those in the Demon Realm.
Before he knew it, adventurers had gathered spontaneously, forming an impromptu massive party.
Barrel was part of that haphazard assembly.
Was it luck or misfortune?
The adventurers who had gathered nearby were all of a similar rank, around rank 5, so they were being shuffled around the difficult parts of the hastily formed defense line.
Barrel considered himself a decent adventurer.
He wasn't recognized as a top-tier rank 6, but he took pride in being someone who could hold his own.
At the same time, he thought he had reached his limit.
So he had been careful not to step into the forest of the Demon Realm, content to secure enough safety and earn his daily bread in the grasslands.
And yet, here he was.
Barrel shouted orders to his fellow adventurers while striking the head of a monster that resembled a human.
He didn't have the luxury to check what type it was.
He recalled the time he had tried to recover the magical stone from a Forest Dragon, but this was far more painful and brutal.
To be honest, he wanted to run away. But if he fled now, that horde of monsters might reach the town.
No, Hekatai would be fine; there was a barrier.
But what about the surrounding area?
What would happen to the nearby villages that had no barriers?
The principles of the Adventurer Guild flashed through Barrel's mind.
For those who couldn't fight. He thought it was a pretty sentiment. He truly believed that.
He had never once risked his life for such a thing, nor did he intend to.
After all, he had become an adventurer because there were no other professions he could take up.
His parents had been killed by monsters or boars, and there was no one to take care of him, so he left the village and became an adventurer.
To Barrel, those who couldn't fight were the ones who hadn't helped him.
He had never risked his life for those people.
But because of that—
Barrel glanced at the faces of the other adventurers who had been caught up in this mess simply because they were nearby.
What the hell. Barrel lamented.
Each of them had the same expression on their faces.
They all wanted to run away, but—
"If I turn tail and run now, I won't be an adventurer, will I!?"
If he fled now, he would become just like those who hadn't helped him.
He couldn't stand that. He absolutely couldn't.
Barrel thought, what the hell is this?
A Great Demon? as he kicked the corpse of the monster that had collapsed on him after he stabbed it in the chest.
"You guys! Get it together! We're pushing back!"
Speaking of which, "the clean-shaven Longdagger" was shouting the same thing.
What were they doing? Well, it didn't matter; they were probably causing a ruckus somewhere.
Barrel wished Shin and the others were here.
But he quickly realized that if they were here, they would likely get caught up in something terrible as well and shouted with a laugh.
"Let's smash the absurdity!"
Adventurers were used to being beaten by death and absurdity.
Then they knew how to fight back.
Barrel and the others raised their fists.
The mountain of magical stone debris clattered and collapsed.
The voice of the figure behind the mask was unrecognizable in terms of gender.
They were probably using the same magical tool as the ones who had attacked when they left the Faltarl capital.
But the body wrapped in the robe had a certain roundness, making it clear that it was a woman.
The one who had kicked the remains of the Great Demon Knight, the pile of magical stone debris, spoke in a flat voice.
"How many of my companions do you think died to bring this here?"
Though the voice was in the form of a question, it was likely not directed at us.
From the tone, I could sense a strong will that did not see us as conversation partners.
So this was a monologue.
A monologue delivered with such volume that it felt like she was speaking to someone, making it all the more eerie.
"Thanks to that, I've had to resort to my last resort. No, it's truly troublesome."
Troublesome, indeed.
The voice carried a tone of something deeply important missing.
Right now, right now, I needed to take that thing's head.
Don't think of it as a person; it's a monster.
So take the initiative and behead it, my instincts as an adventurer screamed inside me.
But I couldn't move.
Because Erika was holding my hand.
The weak grip of her right hand could have been easily shaken off if I wanted to.
But it felt heavier than any chain.
"You must acknowledge it."
A weak voice.
Ah... please.
"This circumstantial evidence, and now the person is right in front of us. There's no way to deny it, is there? Shin."
I understood from her tone that Erika had said she was accustomed to deception, but even so, she had believed, she had wanted to believe.
That Shara had not betrayed them. That the friend she had gained in this new land had not betrayed them.
Ah, please let her be crying.
Wishing for that, I turned around, and then I was betrayed.
Erika wore a smile that resembled a wry grin.
It was the smile of a strong person.
A smile only allowed to those who were strong.
Because they could trample over all the difficulties that fell upon them with their power, they could afford to do so.
Thus, it was only natural for the strong to accept and become accustomed to the difficulties and absurdities that fell upon them.
That smile cut deep into my heart more than her weak voice.
To Erika, who didn't cry, to Erika, who couldn't cry, to the world that made her so, to those who stole her bright future and continued to interfere, a selfish anger welled up.
May you all die.
Alright, I'll kill that thing.
"That thing is different, Erika."
I was surprised by the gentle voice that came from my throat.
"That thing is just an enemy, nothing more. It's not what you think it is."
Erika's hand slipped away.
"You're bad at lying, Shin."
I chose to ignore that voice.
I drew my sword from its sheath and turned to face the masked woman. Her monologue came to a sudden halt.
What had she been saying? Complaining about the world? Complaining about her circumstances?
I understood the meaning, but the voice carried a tone that was fundamentally lacking something, a mechanical curse that had been repeated endlessly.
I had long since tuned it out, so I didn't even remember.
No, there was no need to remember.
She would soon stop speaking anyway.
As I thought that, I noticed the woman moving her hands beneath the robe that enveloped her.
She had said it was her last resort.
Having been attacked by their companions once before, anyone could predict what would happen if it happened again.
Don't think you can do it? I realized I was angrier than I had anticipated.
Why did Shara betray us? Now that I thought about it, it was a question that couldn't be answered.
Was there some reason? I felt a sigh rising at the now irrelevant question, but I bit down on it with my molars.
I was angry; I couldn't help but be angry.
Shara had been there, and Erika had smiled. Shara had been there, and Erika had seemed happy.
The first friend Erika had gained after being exiled was Shara.
Since when had she been betraying us?
The loud, raucous voices, the ill-timed interruptions of our time alone.
Had it all been a lie?
To laugh freely, without any ulterior motives, just because it was fun.
Even in front of the Light Priestess at the academy back home, Erika, who had been a noble daughter, had smiled that way at Shara.
[img]https://i.imgur.com/k0snNoO.jpeg
And I had watched those two... well, yes, it had been fun.
I had been happy.
Instead of a sigh, I bit down on my molars once more.
I would take that head right now; I thought, but my feet wouldn't move.
I was disgusted by my own weakness, and my molars creaked.
Facing Shara, who wore a mask, across the crater created by the Great Demon Knight, I would allow the terrible absurdity of a human turning into a demon.
I couldn't cut her down while she still looked human. I was angry; I was angry at the betraying Shara.
The masked woman with golden hair transformed at a speed that seemed like a joke into a demon with a body that rivaled the Great Demon.
A slick, hairless purple body.
The face that emerged from the cracked mask resembled that of a goat.
A demon—a being different from a monster.
The Church calls them those who have lost the protection of God, but to us adventurers, they are treated as a type of monster that doesn't drop magical stones when defeated.
They occasionally appear, wreak havoc, and are hunted down.
To most people, they are no different from monsters, and many don't even recognize the difference.
However, the scale of the damage they cause is incomparable to that of monsters.
Indeed, monsters will attack if they see a person.
They show no interest in animals other than humans, and they clearly possess hostility only toward humanity.
That is their nature.
But demons, they come looking for humans to kill.
Therefore, we adventurers always kill demons on sight.
If we lack the strength, we even bow our heads to the loathsome nobles to ask for help.
Well, I am a noble myself, though.
"First horses, now goats."
Another characteristic of demons is the instinctive aversion one feels upon seeing them.
A murderous intent that feels like someone is urging me to kill it immediately.
If I let this thing loose in the wild, I wouldn't be able to sleep peacefully.
Just the thought of it being alive and moving somewhere would keep me on edge.
The intense desire to kill it was entirely different from what I felt toward monsters.
I shook my head to dismiss the forced murderous intent that sought to overwhelm my emotions and took a shallow breath.
I clung to it as if I were relying on it.
Otherwise, I would be angry at myself for not being able to cut down Shara.
The opponent had betrayed Erika. I was angry; I was angry at the betraying Shara.
More than that, I was angry at myself for having to kill Shara.
The absurdity of a human becoming a demon was nothing compared to that anger.
"Shara... why?"
With Erika's voice coming from behind me, I finally steeled my resolve.
As a tentacle fell from the side of the goat demon, I raised the intensity of my body enhancement to the maximum.
I clung to the instinctive aversion to demons, channeling it into my murderous intent.
The unpleasant sensation of my vision narrowing, everything felt wrong.
So this is definitely not a sigh.
The breath escaping through the gaps of my clenched molars mixed with magical power.
I finally steeled myself; I was going to kill Shara.
My right foot stepped forward, a rough advance pulled by my murderous intent dug into the ground.
In my line of sight stood the goat demon, readying itself.
Erika murmured from behind, "Shara, you didn't have to turn into a hairless goat."
And then Shara screamed.
"Got you!"
In an instant, I slipped on the ground, and the goat demon, who had swung its tentacles wildly from a distance, awkwardly pulled them back.
I exposed my face, sliding across a third of the crater, displaying the worst possible embarrassment as I lifted my head from the ground, contemplating how to apologize.
Just then, Shara, who had emerged from the forest, pointed at me and shouted again.
"Shin-san, what are you doing all of a sudden!? I can cry too, you know!?"
I couldn't quite imagine why Shara would cry for a different reason than Erika.
Thinking that, I became convinced.
Ah, I've really messed up, haven't I?
The real Shara, who had emerged from the forest, pointed at me as she slid down the crater and marched toward me at a brisk pace.
Amazing, Shara; she wasn't even paying any attention to the demon.
I just got punched by Shin-san!
I'm all alone in the mid-level of the Demon Realm!
And now a ton of dirt and wood is falling from the sky!
What is going on!?
What is going on!?
Shara screamed, her complaints taking the form of questions. Remarkably, even the goat demon seemed bewildered.
Seeing that if I stayed on the ground, I would end up in a mount position, with my neck grabbed and shaken, I hurriedly stood up.
Am I an idiot?
I was prioritizing avoiding being mounted by Shara over the goat demon.
"You will explain this to me! No matter how much of a barbarian Shin-san is, you can at least explain!"
Who’s a barbarian?
I thought as I almost retorted, feeling guilty for my actions, but Shara's outburst was cut off by Erika.
Just as Shara, clearly (mainly towards me) wanting to say more, took a breath to shout again, Erika hugged her.
It was a hug that felt like a running start.
I was impressed by Shara's strength, as she didn't fall over.
"Ugh! Erika? Huh? What? Why are you hugging me?"
Shara, who had swallowed her scream in surprise at Erika's sudden hug, was confused.
"I'm so glad... I'm really glad..."
"Well, if you were that worried, you shouldn't have punched me in the first place."
"That's not what I meant..."
Erika gently released her embrace.
Shara seemed a bit down, realizing she hadn't been worried about at all.
"It's all Shin's fault."
I felt the anger in Shara reignite at Erika's words.
Before she could shout again, I apologized.
"I'm sorry! I thought Shara had betrayed us!"
I said it with enough force, hoping it would just flow over, but Shara's eyebrows shot up.
"Why on earth did you think that—"
You thought I betrayed you? was what she wanted to say, but I cut her off before she could finish.
There was no time left.
"I'm really sorry! I mistook you for that thing!"
I pointed my thumb at the source of the murderous intent swelling behind me.
Shara's gaze shot to the back of me.
"Wait! That's a demon!"
Ah, she hadn't even noticed the demon in her anger directed at me.
I thought as I watched Shara shout.
Amazing, since Shara showed up, none of the three of us had been paying attention to the demon.
Despite having transformed into a demon as a last resort, it had been left unattended, and it looked like it was trembling with rage.
The atmosphere had turned
"normal,
" and even though it wasn't a scene for smiles, I almost found myself grinning.
Shara was terrifying.
But well, at this point, it was impossible to fight that thing, so I moved in front of Erika and Shara to regroup.
Shara pointed at the demon with her right hand and shouted.
"Gross! That thing is gross!"
Shara's vocabulary, which summarized that fundamental aversion to the demon with just one word, made me think she was an idiot.
The first time I fought a demon was three years ago.
At that time, facing a monster for the first time, I had been overwhelmed by the murderous intent that felt like a mission to kill the being before me.
Yet she was dismissing it with just "gross." Was Shara amazing or an idiot?
No, it was definitely the latter.
Even so, I thought, "Yeah, that is gross."
Last time it was a horse, and this time it's a goat.
Do demons need to have hooves or something?
Ah, but still, it was disgusting.
It seemed I wasn't the only one feeling that way; Erika was also frowning as she looked at the now towering goat demon that rivaled the Great Demon.
Its surface was a flat purple color, devoid of any biological wrinkles, and the tentacles sprouting from its sides felt entirely unnatural.
It wasn't about the shape; its very existence was repulsive.
Shara, who had been repeating "gross," suddenly fell silent.
"Did I get mistaken for that thing!?"
Now, how was I going to fight that thing?
"What do you mean!? Are you saying I look like that thing to you, Shin-san!?"
Last time, the horse-faced demon had thrown me after I was surprised by a human turning into a demon, and if I charged straight at it, I would be blown away.
It wasn't a normal opponent to let my guard down against.
In terms of strength, it was likely stronger than the Forest Dragon.
"Why are you ignoring me!? Explain! I demand an explanation! As a maiden!"
